Earlier recovery repairs and their bounded native proof remain valid. **Priority:** P1 **Reviewed head:** `47aa7daa495e526b9cbef71d77ab77f105b44fa2` **Owner decision:** Required. That proof stands, but does not cover the newly identified Linux planning defect or establish complete published-driver qualification. | | **Patch quality** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | 1 actionable review finding remain. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Verified | Sufficient (live_output): The recorded native component run exercises retained-service restoration and final-effect rejection after lease revocation, executor replacement, and service reassignment; the inspected authority/restoration modules remain unchanged. That proof stands, but does not cover the newly identified Linux planning defect or establish complete published-driver qualification. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 10 items | Introduced Linux planning defect: The new canRebind condition rejects the presence of managedOverrides or managedDefinition. Ordinary canonical systemd units carry both fields, including managedOverrides: {}, so eligible split-prefix updates select the old service root instead of rebinding.
Canonical systemd metadata contract: The systemd reader includes the managed definition and override metadata for canonical user units; its drop-in reader deliberately returns an empty object when no overrides exist. Existing override helpers distinguish this from an operator override.
Same assumption in retained recovery: Original-service observation rejects either metadata field at lines 263–270, and original-definition restoration repeats that rejection at line 58. Repairing only planning would therefore expose a later refusal; the owning paths need one consistent interpretation. | | **Findings** | 1 actionable finding | [P1] Recognize known-empty systemd metadata before rejecting rebinds | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together The updater coordinates package installation, Node selection, Doctor maintenance, and the operating system's Gateway service. It must preserve service ownership and operator state while activating or recovering an installation. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Update request and installed packages] --> B[Inspect Node and Gateway ownership] B --> C{Service can be rebound} C -->|Yes| D[Prepare invoking installation] C -->|No| E[Update existing service installation] D --> F[Activate under live ownership] E --> F F --> G{Gateway healthy} G -->|Yes| H[Complete update] G -->|No| I[Restore verified original service] ``` ## Decision needed | Question | Recommendation | |---|---| | After the Linux metadata defect is repaired, must the current candidate complete published-driver qualification before landing, or may this land as a bounded component improvement? | **Complete upgrade qualification:** Require a current published-driver compatibility result before accepting the broader upgrade claim. | Why: Root policy requires published-driver upgrade evidence, while the body explicitly defers that qualification; the prior review requested a landing disposition that remains unresolved. ## Before merge - [ ] **Recognize known-empty systemd metadata before rejecting rebinds (P1)** - For an ordinary canonical Linux user unit with no drop-ins, `readSystemdServiceExecStart` returns `managedDefinition` and `managedOverrides: {}`. Both are truthy, so these checks always disable the intended A-to-B rebind and update A instead, leaving the CLI/Gateway prefix mismatch. The Linux planner test omits these real reader fields. Interpret the canonical override contract consistently here and in the matching observation/restoration guards; preserve genuinely overridden definitions. This was missed in the previous review: the implicated code is unchanged since `af393400847ade886087c4dde230ee53e5dd556c`. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The complete published-driver-to-current-candidate upgrade remains unqualified: older drivers choose their target before candidate code runs, and prior evidence includes both successful service-root updating and pre-activation refusal. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The bounded native recovery evidence does not establish broader platform or schema-changing upgrade recovery; installations whose retained runtime cannot read migrated state may still require operator recovery. - [ ] **Complete next step (P2)** - Correct known-empty systemd metadata handling across planning and recovery, then record the maintainer's disposition of the published-driver qualification limits. - [ ] **Resolve maintainer decision** - Resolve the maintainer decision shown above before merge. - [ ] **Review config compatibility** - Confirm compatibility and upgrade impact for the changed config or default surface before merge. - [ ] **Add data-model compatibility proof** - Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge. ## Findings - [P1] Recognize known-empty systemd metadata before rejecting rebinds — `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-service-plan.ts:605-610`

## L147 installed-update qualification — `482c140ab372304208b8791265d71152efd303d3`

The requested Node 22 baseline cannot be installed normally: published `openclaw@2026.9.4` requires `>=24.16.0 <25 || >=26.1.0`, and its preinstall exited 1 on Node 22.23.2. No engine/lifecycle guard was bypassed. The executable comparison used checksum-verified Node 24.20.0 (service prefix A) and Node 26.8.2 (invoking CLI prefix B), with real Linux arm64 systemd-user Gateways in disposable containers. Over 130 GiB remained free. All config and workspace data are synthetic.

Candidate built from the exact head with:

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline
pnpm build
node scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs --skip-build --allow-unreleased-changelog \
  --output-dir .local/l147/candidate --output-name candidate.tgz
```

Build and canonical package integrity verification passed. Tarball SHA-256: `637fe883994d27cab7dc1e8a3ec0c0e6eaa5b1dfe3b3e88f1851e0aa8186ade1`. Version metadata was not relabeled; build metadata identifies the exact PR head.

### (a) Published-driver handoff

Both prefixes initially contained npm `openclaw@2026.9.4` (`3a9d69db306c`). The loaded service definition pointed at A's Node and package; the shell selected B. Baseline readiness and Doctor passed.

```sh
PATH=/home/node/.nvm/versions/node/v26.8.2/bin:/usr/bin:/bin \
  openclaw update --yes --tag file:/proof/candidate/candidate.tgz --json
```

Observed: update exit **0**, target **A**, candidate build installed in **A**, B still published `3a9d69db306c`. The service restarted against A's candidate package, using the available system Node 24.20.0; it did **not** rebind to B. `/readyz` passed; Doctor from A's candidate exited **0**. Doctor from B's still-published CLI exited **1** because the active candidate migrated the agent database to schema 20 and the published CLI supports 19.
